page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server configured with 12 vCPUs derived from 6 dedicated physical cores on a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. Operating on KVM virtualization across an x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 48 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and AES. Memory capacity is provisioned at 96 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation suited for data footprints that exceed standard general-purpose distributions. The instance includes 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and omits local storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize network-attached cloud disks.

Benchmark results place the processor and memory subsystem consistently in the middle quartile of cloud hardware. In stress-ng evaluations, the server delivered a single-core score of 1867.88 and a multi-core score of 11629.58, accompanied by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7628.0. Uncached large-block memory throughput reaches 40.39 GB/sec for reads and 41.96 GB/sec for writes, which translates to a Redis SET benchmark throughput of 11.89 million operations per second. Conversely, compute-intensive execution patterns with large weights scale poorly; prompt processing and generation for 7B parameter models recorded lower-quartile performance at 24.07 and 8.09 tokens per second, confirming that parallel mathematical execution is restricted compared to accelerated hardware.

Cost efficiency is optimized for environments where memory capacity is the governing design metric rather than raw disk IOPS or accelerated matrix computation. Because the hardware profile does not bundle local NVMe drives, architectural overhead remains focused on memory allocation rather than idle internal disk channels. Appropriate enterprise workloads include in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, operational caching infrastructure, medium-tier relational database instances, and extract-transform-load (ETL) staging environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.3xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance configured with 12 vCPUs and 96 GB of memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a 2.7 GHz base clock with dedicated thread mapping, the architecture supplies 48 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. With zero local storage bundled and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, instances require network-attached block storage for persistent data. Benchmark metrics position the server in the middle tiers across raw compute and memory bandwidth, recording 40.39 GB/sec in large-block memory read bandwidth and 11.89 million operations per second on Redis SET evaluations. Larger computational tasks such as 7B model inference reveal CPU throughput constraints, yielding bottom-quartile throughput. The resource profile proves cost-efficient for memory-constrained workloads that do not demand persistent local disk, specifically in-memory key-value stores, distributed database nodes, and caching infrastructure.
